From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an initial workbook (attached) with conservative and optimistic lanes for the pilot traffic profile you shared. High-level summary here — please treat numbers as preliminary until we validate with a short sim run: 

- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted 8-bit quantized variant): conservative = 275k tokens per $1, optimistic = 390k tokens per $1. These assume average 1.2k token contexts and 120-token responses.
- Caching impact: prefix/KV cache expected to reduce generation tokens by ~18–26% for repeat patient Q&A (measured on our pilot trace sample). We included both a no-cache and 20% cache lanes in the workbook.
- Batching: we modeled two batching regimes: low-latency (micro-batch ~1–2 requests, preserves p95 < 220ms) and throughput (batch sizes 8–12, improves tokens/$ by ~22% but increases p95 to ~420ms). Workbook has the breakpoints and switching policy we recommend.
- Fallbacks: autopilot routing to quantized CPU-safe variant increases tokens/$ by ~40% (worse) but preserves availability. We included cost delta and suggested MAP escalation thresholds (if 5-minute rolling CPU fallback > 3% of requests, trigger capacity ramp).

Action items I'm proposing for the MAP addendum: 
1) We validate with a 48-hour traffic replay (you provide anonymized trace subset) — results added to workbook.
2) Redwood provides a canary config mapping: (a) initial pilot variant + batching policy, (b) fallback variant and auto-failover SLOs.
3) Finance signoff on the final tokens/$ lane and PO terms.

I've attached: redwood_map_token_econ_workbook.xlsx (tabs: summary, sims, batch-policy, caching-assumptions) and a small prefeth-sim csv sample. Can Neha own the traffic replay and sim outputs, and Jordan own the MAP wording for procurement?

Regards,
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
